ab.seg: ⁊ man singe ælc Frigdæge æt ælcum mynstre ealle þa Godes þeowan an fiftig for þone cyng ⁊ for ealle þe willaþ ðæt he wile ⁊ for þa oþre, swa hy geearnian.
And mon singe ylce Frigdæge æt ylcum mynstre ealle ða Goddes ðeowas an fiftig sealmas for ðone cyng ⁊ for ealle ða ðe willen þæt he wille ⁊ for ða oþre, swa hi swa geearnigen.
And ylce man ðe wille mot gebeten ylce gestale wiþ ðone teonde butan ylcum wite oþ gongdagas; ⁊ beo syþþan swa hit ær wæs.
Et decantetur omni die Ueneris in singulis ecclesiis unum quinquagenarium (psalmorum) pro rege et omni populo, qui uult quod ipse.
⁊ man singe ælc Frigdæge æt ælcum mynstre ealle þa Godes þeowan an fiftig [sealmas] for þone cyng ⁊ for ealle þe willaþ ðæt he wile ⁊ for þa oþre, swa hy geearnian.
[And ylce man ðe wille mot gebeten ylce gestale wiþ ðone teonde butan ylcum wite oþ gong-dagas; ⁊ beo syþþan swa hit ær wæs.]
Und man singe, alle Gottesdiener, jeden Freitag in jeder Stiftskirche einen Funfziger [Psalmen] für den König und für alle, die wollen, was er will, und für die anderen, je wie sie es verdienen.

(3, 1. Und jedermann, der will, darf jeden Diebstahl ohne jede Strafe, [nur] dem Kläger gegenüber büssen [von heute] bis zu den Processionstagen; weiterhin jedoch bleibe es [das Strafrecht], wie es zuvor gewesen ist. Ld)
And let all the servants of God sing, every Friday in every minster, a fifty [of psalms] for the king and for all who will what he wills, and for the others, according as they deserve it.

(And everyone who wishes may compensate for any theft without any fine, [only] to the plaintiff, [from today] until the Rogation days; thereafter, however, let it [the penal law] remain as it was before. Ld)

And in every monastery, all the servants of God shall sing every Friday fifty psalms for the king, and for all who are minded to carry out his wishes. And [they shall sing psalms] for these others according to their merits.

And every man who so wishes may pay to his accuser compensation for every theft, without any manner of fine, until Rogation days. But after that it [the fine] shall be [paid], as it has been in the past.
And every Friday at every minster all the servants of God are to sing 50 psalms for the king and for all who desire what he desires, and for the others, as they may deserve.
And every man who wishes may compensate the accuser for every theft until Rogation days, without fine; after that it is to be as it was before.

Jeder treue Untertan heisst qui uelit quod rex IV As 6, 3; gemeint scheint nicht bloss sein Gefolge weitesten Sinnes, samt hohem Klerus und Beamten; denn des Herrn Willen zu wollen versprach der Untertan als Königstreue (s. d. Gl 7 b) nach Muster des Mannschaftseides; s. d. Gl 2; Gefolgsadel 20. — ‘will, dass er König sei’ missversteht Br

Every loyal subject is called qui uelit quod rex in IV As 6, 3; what seems to be meant is not merely his following in the widest sense, including the higher clergy and officials; for the subject promised, as part of loyalty to the king (see that word in Gl 7 b), to will his lord's will, on the model of the oath of vassalage; see that word in Gl 2; Gefolgsadel 20. — Br misunderstands it as ‘wishes that he be king’

Der Satz fehlt H Q und stand also nicht in lq, geschweige im Archetyp. Er ist wahrscheinlich, wie sicher der Zusatz, den hier H anknüpft (IV As 6), Bruchstück eines Æthelstanschen Gesetzes. Die sprachliche Modernisierung und Verderbnis fallen wie in Ld’s früheren Kapiteln dem Schreiber und Drucker zur Last

The sentence is lacking in H Q and so did not stand in lq, let alone in the archetype. It is probably, as the addition that H attaches here (IV As 6) certainly is, a fragment of a law of Æthelstan. The linguistic modernisation and corruption are to be laid at the door of the scribe and the printer, as in Ld's earlier chapters
Also ohne Justizertrag für den Richter; s. Gl Amnestie 2. 3. Kurz darauf gewährte der König eine ähnliche Erlassung des Strafgeldes bis August: III As 3
Thus without judicial profit for the judge; see Gl Amnestie 2. 3. Shortly afterwards the king granted a similar remission of fines until August: III As 3
Vgl. Gl Bittfahrtstage 3. a
Cf. Gl Bittfahrtstage 3. a

That is to say, that the suit might be settled privately out of court, and then no fine would be paid to the judge. Ine, cap. 52, expressly forbids such private settlements. ‘These secret compositions,’ says Thorpe (p. 134), ‘are forbidden by nearly every early code of Europe; for by such a proceeding both the judge and the crown lost their profits’ (cf. III As. cap. 3).
Cf. Alf. cap. 5 § 5; II As. cap. 13.
